text:
Maria Nguyen: Heads up — us-east1 nvme nodes are spiking read-retries during GPU provisioning. Attach queue jumped to ~220 and a bunch of preemptible jobs are stuck.
Alex Li: Noticed the same after the kernel rollout yesterday to that fleet. Kernel logs show repeated nvme aborts, could be a scheduler/firmware interaction.
Maria Nguyen: Sample kernel lines:
```
Mar 21 12:03:11 host kernel: nvme0: abort status: 0x8 qid 1 cid 42 
Mar 21 12:03:12 host kernel: nvme0: read-retry count=4 lba=0x1f2b3 
Mar 21 12:03:12 host kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1234567
```
Sasha Patel: Can we pull SMART + iostat for a few nodes and confirm it's wear vs transient backlog? Also which OS/image and scrub version? Is janitor running heavy scrubs right now?
Alex Li: Running: `smartctl -A /dev/nvme0 && iostat -x 1 3` on a repro host shows high svc_t and avgqu-sz spikes. Image is infra-image-2026-03-10, janitor v2.4 with default concurrency 6.
InfraBot: :warning: Alert: GPU-attach-queue length=223 in us-east1. Auto-escalation scheduled in 10m if no mitigation.
Rajiv K: I can throttle janitor scrubs for that region for 20m to test impact. Tradeoff: we'll delay cleanup and potentially increase ephemeral capacity pressure, but it should relieve foreground attach IO.
Maria Nguyen: Do it. Also, can we temporarily route new GPU attaches to the cold-dedicated pool for the rollout window? We want to avoid user-visible errors.
Sasha Patel: Pushing scrub rate cap now: `region.us-east1.janitor.scrub_concurrency=2` — flipping in 30s. I'll also enable health-probe sampling at 0.5s for nvme read-retry detection.
Alex Li: After throttle, iostat shows iops down ~38% and avgqu-sz reduced. Attach queue dropped to ~60 after ~8 minutes. Looks promising.
Maria Nguyen: Good. Long-term proposals: 1) per-node janitor cap (2-3), 2) health-based transient quarantine when read-retry > 3 in 1m (auto-reassign), 3) fallback routing: route attaches to cold pool for 30m windows during fleet-wide scrub waves. We should also audit firmware mix in us-east1.
Oncall Pager: Added runbook note and PagerDuty playbook entry for "nvme read-retry cascade". Escalation threshold set: queue > 500. I'll keep monitoring the channel.
Rajiv K: I'll open a follow-up ticket with the TTL for the throttled window, expected cloud cost delta, and a quick roll plan for per-node caps.
Maria Nguyen: Thanks all — I'll collate logs and numbers into the ticket. If anyone sees read-retry climb again, ping @Oncall Pager immediately.
Alex Li: :thumbsup:
